chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Nadr, from (Abi Sayyar) Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in a sermon: 'Shall I not inform you of the best of creation in this world and the Hereafter? It is forgiveness towards those who wrong you, doing good to those who do evil to you, and giving to those who deprive you.'
And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'In mutual hatred is the severer of hair; I do not mean the severing of hair [through shaving], but I mean the severing of faith.'

key_terms.الْحَالِقَةُ: The severer / That which shaves off

ai.seo_question: What are the best qualities of creation according to the Prophet's sermon in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates *sabr* and *ihsan* to the pinnacle of spiritual excellence, framing forgiveness and generosity as the defining traits of the 'best of creation.' The metaphor of 'hair-cutting' (*al-haliqua*) serves as a profound scholarly commentary on how mutual hatred erodes the visible and invisible bonds of the community, effectively severing the roots of faith (*din*) just as a razor cuts hair.
